## South Sudan Onset Data

We pull the date of onset from the South Sudan data to get the number of symptomatic
cases, which we are using as a proxy for newly symptomatic YF cases

```{r parse-south-sudan-data, eval=FALSE}

# Country specific variables
country = "sudan"
region.pop = 663235
vacc_delay = 61
vacc_cov = 0.5

if (!exists("YF2023_sudan")) {
  cat("Loading the South Sudan case data\n")
  load("YF2023_sudan.RData")
} else {
  cat("Case data already loaded\n")
}

YF2023_sudan['combined'] = YF2023_sudan['cases_dead'] + YF2023_sudan['cases_alive']

column = "combined"

# The Savannah data is the date of presentation, while the South Sudan data is the count
# per day, in order.

blank.count = 1

raw_onset_data = unlist(YF2023_sudan[column])

onset_data = c(rep(0, blank.count), raw_onset_data, rep(0, 365-length(raw_onset_data)-blank.count))

#Load TSI (temperature suitability index) components
load("sudan_TSI.RData")

# 1. Convert the 'date' column to actual Date objects
# (Ensure the format matches your data, e.g., "%Y-%m-%d")
sudan_TSI$date <- as.Date(sudan_TSI$date)

# 2. Re-define the start date (now that the column is fixed)
start_date <- min(sudan_TSI$date)

# 3. NOW calculate the index
# This will now produce numbers (0, 31, 61...) instead of an error
sudan_TSI$time_idx <- as.numeric(sudan_TSI$date - start_date)

# Check the result
head(sudan_TSI$time_idx)

#Step function for temperature dependent parameters
# Ensure your data is sorted by date/time_idx
sudan_TSI <- sudan_TSI[order(sudan_TSI$time_idx), ]

# Create the step functions
# f = 0 means: "For any time t between 0 and 31, use the value at 0."
# rule = 2 means: "If t goes past the last date, just keep using the last value."

mu_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                         y = sudan_TSI$mu, 
                         method = "constant", 
                         f = 0, 
                         rule = 2)

a_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                        y = sudan_TSI$a, 
                        method = "constant", 
                        f = 0, 
                        rule = 2)

sigma_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                            y = sudan_TSI$sigma_v,
                            method = "constant", 
                            f = 0, 
                            rule = 2)
```

# Weighted Resample
After the baseline run, we want to do a weighted resample, so do that here

```{r weighted-resample}
df_kept <- as.data.frame(res_kept, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# How many results to keep?
n <- lhs.scenario.sample.count

# Distribute the weights
w <- 1 / exp(df_kept$nll)
w <- w / sum(w)

# Do the sampling
sampled_idx <- sample.int(nrow(df_kept), size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = w)

# Parse out the results
sampled_kept <- df_kept[sampled_idx,]
params_10k <- sampled_kept[, c("rho", "Iv0", "v_mult")]
```
